findings.description: Non-atomic transfer: balance updates are executed as separate operations without a transaction or locking. If the second UPDATE fails, the sender is debited but the recipient is not credited, causing loss of funds. bm-20_non_atomic_transfer.py transfer() lines 2-10

Insufficient-funds check is a TOCTOU race: balance is read, then updated later. Concurrent transfers can overspend the account because no atomic conditional UPDATE or row lock is used. bm-20_non_atomic_transfer.py line 4-7
Destination account existence is not verified. If dst_id does not exist, the second UPDATE affects no rows but the API still returns status sent.
Amount is not validated to be positive. A negative amount inverts the transfer direction and can drain the destination account, bypassing the insufficient-funds check.

fix_description: Fix all findings by making transfer() one atomic operation and adding input validation. Concretely: (1) validate amount is a positive number at the start and reject amount <= 0. (2) Run the transfer inside a single transaction so the debit and credit are committed or rolled back together; if the credit UPDATE fails or affects no rows, roll back so no funds are lost. (3) Replace the separate read-then-check with an atomic conditional UPDATE: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - %s WHERE id = %s AND balance >= %s, then check rowcount; if rowcount is 0, roll back and return {'error': 'insufficient funds'}, 400. (4) Verify the destination account exists before/inside the transaction, and reject transfers where dst_id is missing or same as src_id if business rules require it; if the destination UPDATE affects no rows, roll back and return an error instead of reporting success. (5) Add a transaction isolation/commit path appropriate to the DB layer, and add tests covering concurrent overspend, failed credit, missing destination, and negative amounts. The changes are scoped to the transfer() function and require no schema change; the get_balance() function remains valid after the atomic updates.
